papers.title: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?

summary.tldr: A study on multi-agent LLM deliberation shows that agent defection rates rise linearly with the proportion of deceivers, with LLMs succumbing to deceptive minorities unlike humans.
key_points: Susceptibility to deception scales with the proportion of deceptive agents rather than the total group size.
The defection rate—honest agents switching to incorrect answers—increases linearly as the proportion of deceivers grows.
Unlike humans, who typically conform only when deceivers form a majority, LLM agents regularly defect when deceivers are a minority.
Susceptibility varies based on model pairings, particularly the specific model used for the honest agent.
Allowing deceptive agents to coordinate privately unexpectedly reduces their effectiveness in swaying the group.
summary.why_it_matters: Simply scaling group size does not protect multi-agent LLM systems against adversarial subversion, as adversaries only need to maintain their proportion within the group.

papers.title: GHOST-Q: Towards Studying Grounding Hallucinations Overlooked Under Same-score TradeOffs in Quantized VLMS

summary.tldr: GHOST-Q evaluates 8B vision-language models across FP16, INT8, and NF4 precisions, revealing significant grounding hallucinations and generation budget censoring despite quantized variants maintaining baseline accuracy scores.
key_points: Evaluated three 8B VLM families across FP16, INT8, and NF4 precisions on utility and hallucination-sensitive benchmarks.
Five of six quantized variants kept aggregate MMStar accuracy within +/-2 percentage points of FP16.
Item-by-item pairing showed 10 of 36 effects remained significant post-FDR correction, with nine occurring on hallucination-sensitive conditions.
A100 profiling showed memory reductions do not guarantee latency drops, while an AMBER audit revealed architecture- and precision-dependent generation budget censoring.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating quantized VLMs solely on aggregate accuracy scores risks masking critical visual grounding failures, hallucination risks, and unexpected latency bottlenecks in production deployments.

papers.title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: TRACE is an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack that autoregressively reconstructs private observation-action trajectories from policy gradients in distributed embodied reinforcement learning.
key_points: Exploits cross-time correlation between consecutive gradients and utilizes closed-form action recovery from policy-head gradients, proven exact for small entropy regularization.
Achieves 18.8 dB PSNR with near-perfect action recovery at 3-4.5 ms per frame, outperforming single-frame and optimization-based attacks in speed and quality.
Demonstrates broad transferability across recurrent, residual, and compact transformer architectures, multi-modal inputs, and large discrete action spaces.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard gradient-sharing mechanisms in embodied RL fail to protect sensor data, indicating that future privacy defenses must be sequence-aware to prevent trajectory leakage.

papers.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers

summary.tldr: A latent dynamics framework aligns autoencoders for long-horizon stability using Koopman learning, noise injection, and multi-step fine-tuning, reducing rollout error by 40% over standard reconstruction-only models.
key_points: Identifies that long-horizon autoregressive instability stems from latent spaces optimized purely for single-frame reconstruction rather than dynamical evolution.
Combines Koopman operator learning and Hamming noise injection during autoencoder training with noise injection and multi-step rollout fine-tuning during dynamics training.
Shows that interventions improving long-term rollout stability frequently degrade short-term reconstruction and single-step prediction metrics.
Matches or exceeds full-resolution model accuracy on two physics benchmarks while using 100x fewer FLOPs and 50% less GPU memory.
Demonstrates stable extrapolation on mesoscale crystal-plasticity fatigue simulations over time horizons orders of magnitude past the training window.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that latent representations must be engineered specifically for temporal dynamics rather than pure spatial compression to build stable, computationally efficient neural surrogate solvers.

papers.title: Aim Short to Reach Far: Your Frozen World Model Can Plan Better Than You Think

summary.tldr: Anchored Planning improves visual world model control by directing a frozen LeWM model toward short-horizon intermediate targets retrieved from past experience rather than scoring directly against the distant final goal image.
key_points: Scoring actions solely against a final goal image fails when optimal trajectories temporarily move away from the goal in observation space.
Anchored Planning retrieves an observed segment matching current and goal states, then directs the planner toward an intermediate target shortly after the segment's start.
The method improves action synthesis and recorded-action ranking on Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom environments without additional model training.
Performance depends on target distance horizon and progressively shrinking the retrieval span as execution advances, outperforming final-goal search.
Lower successor-prediction error in world models does not inherently correlate with better downstream control performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Visual world models can solve complex, long-horizon tasks without costly retraining by simply altering the planning target to short-term intermediate goals.

papers.title: Let Training Guide Selection: Online Synthetic Data Filtering via Real-Anchored Utility

summary.tldr: FROST is an online framework that dynamically filters synthetic data using gradient feedback anchored in real training data, eliminating the need for external verifiers or held-out validation sets.
key_points: Estimates synthetic data utility using gradient feedback anchored directly to real training data.
Calibrates batch utility against recent training history to decide 'when' to filter and removes low-utility samples from out-of-band batches to decide 'what' to retain.
Filters out approximately 20-30% of synthetic data while improving real-task downstream performance.
Validated across image classification, LLM fine-tuning for text-to-SQL, and a large-scale industrial ads re-ranking production system.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables models to selectively discard unhelpful or noisy synthetic samples on the fly, improving performance without requiring expensive manual annotations, external verifiers, or separate validation sets.

papers.title: CORDIAL: Calibrating Ordinal LLM Outputs from Few Labels

summary.tldr: CORDIAL calibrates ordinal LLM output distributions using a five-parameter channel that preserves first-order stochastic order and requires only a handful of labeled examples to infer its posterior.
key_points: Uses a five-parameter channel model to correct noisy, saturated, compressed, or biased LLM probability distributions over ordered scales.
Proves theoretically that the channel transformation preserves first-order stochastic order.
Achieved the lowest log loss in 76 out of 80 tested settings (using Amazon reviews, CMU-MOSEI, and four LLMs) with sample sizes ranging from 5 to 100 labels.
With a 7B parameter LLM and 20 labels, CORDIAL matched the log-loss performance of the top baseline that required 28 to 54 labels.

Enables learning priors across different tasks and fusing predictions from multiple LLMs, with unrestricted baselines like Dirichlet calibration only outperforming it when label counts reach hundreds or thousands.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces the amount of labeled data required to calibrate LLM probability outputs on ordinal tasks, matching complex baselines with less than half the training labels.

papers.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models

summary.tldr: Researchers show that short, natural context additions can flip correct choices in dedicated decision models like Jev to high-confidence wrong options without changing the gold answer.
key_points: Using option probabilities, an optimizer refined context additions within 64 evaluations per item while preserving the source, question, choices, and gold answer.
On the Jev model, optimized contexts flipped 312 out of 508 initially correct decisions (61.4%), with 229 cases assigning at least 0.7 probability to the target wrong option.
Across seven datasets, three other decision systems exhibited targeted flip rates ranging from 64.9% to 73.2% on initially correct decisions.
summary.why_it_matters: This extreme sensitivity to surrounding context highlights the risks of using language-based decision model probability outputs as reliable interfaces for automated downstream routing and action execution.

papers.title: Multimodal Thinking with Renderable Programs

summary.tldr: SVGLM enables vision-language models to incorporate images into their reasoning chains by generating renderable, scalable vector graphics (SVG) text primitives during the thought process.
key_points: Uses SVG primitives to leverage their duality as both textual instructions and rendered vector images.
Provides a compact, interpretable alternative to rasterized or latent image representations in reasoning chains.
Includes a large curated dataset for SVG-based image editing and a paradigm for fine-tuning open-source VLMs.
Demonstrates SVG generation and image-based reasoning performance on a mathematical reasoning benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: SVG primitives offer a tractable, text-compatible medium for digital agents to perform visual reasoning without relying on complex pixel-level or latent generation.

papers.title: MILO: Efficient Many-shot In-Context Learning with Block-wise Low-rank Compression

summary.tldr: MILO is a context compression framework that applies block-wise low-rank KV cache compression and entropy-based dynamic rank allocation for efficient many-shot in-context learning.
key_points: MILO targets the KV cache memory bottleneck caused by thousands of demonstration examples in many-shot in-context learning.
It implements block-wise low-rank compression, grouping multiple demonstration examples into distinct blocks.
It dynamically allocates rank budgets across blocks based on information entropy to account for heterogeneous context density.
Evaluations on Qwen2.5 models demonstrate up to a 50% KV cache memory reduction and a 1.8x throughput improvement with negligible accuracy loss on classification and reasoning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: MILO significantly reduces memory overhead and boosts throughput for long-context LLM inference, facilitating scalable online serving and on-device deployment.

papers.title: TimeBraid: Unifying Time Series and Language for Understanding and Forecasting

summary.tldr: TimeBraid is a model family that unifies pretrained language and time-series foundation models into a shared representation space using interleaved global residual attention layers for joint understanding and forecasting.
key_points: Aligns pretrained language models and pretrained time-series foundation models via interleaved global residual attention layers.
Utilizes a unified prompting scheme to handle diverse time-series and text tasks across both modalities.
Trained using stabilized joint optimization on a dataset of 2.2M curated series-text pairs and 4.9M instruction-tuning samples.
Performs competitively on benchmarks for time-series perception, reasoning, and both context-aided and unimodal forecasting against task-specific and larger models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables a single unified architecture to perform time-series forecasting, temporal reasoning, and natural language instruction following without relying on task-specific models.

papers.title: C3M: Cross-Session Multimodal Memory Maintenance for Long-Horizon Tasks

summary.tldr: C3M is a cross-session multimodal memory architecture that maintains a bounded active index over persistent text-image evidence using relation-aware updates and budgeted query-time routing.
key_points: Maintains a bounded, query-blind active index linked to persistent source text-image evidence to preserve temporal distinctions and provenance.
Uses relation-aware updates to consolidate redundant information while explicitly retaining complementary and incompatible records.
Employs budgeted routing at query time to select relevant index pages and expand source evidence within a fixed reader budget.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-horizon AI agents to retain precise visual and textual evidence across multiple sessions without exceeding fixed memory limits or discarding critical fine-grained details.

papers.title: IterSynth: Rethinking Deep Search Agents via Role-Decoupled Iterative Synthesis

summary.tldr: IterSynth replaces ReAct with a role-decoupled search framework that alternates between a Planner and a Synthesizer using an evolving summary state to reduce context noise.
key_points: Decouples deep search into a Planner for identifying information needs and a Synthesizer for integrating evidence into a persistent, evolving summary state.
Eliminates growing context noise by using the updated summary state instead of accumulating full search histories.
Introduces Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization (RDPO) for reinforcement learning, combining terminal outcome rewards with turn-level rubric evaluations for role-specific credit assignment.
IterSynth-8B achieves an average score of 50.7 across five long-horizon benchmarks (including BrowseComp and Xbench-DS), outperforming the top sub-8B baseline by +4.2%.
Functions as a model-agnostic prompting strategy that provides zero-shot improvements over ReAct on proprietary frontier models.
summary.why_it_matters: IterSynth improves LLM search agent accuracy and efficiency by decoupling planning from synthesis and preventing performance degradation caused by bloated context windows.

papers.title: Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe

summary.tldr: Rufus-Air introduces an open, eight-stage post-training recipe for GLM-4.5-Air-Base (106B-A12B) that relies entirely on open-source components, public data, and verifiable-to-soft reward ordering without new human annotations.
key_points: Executes an eight-stage serial pipeline: SFT, Reasoning RL, Coding RL, Instruction-Following RL, General Agent, Coding Agent, Search Agent, and RLHF.
Applies difficulty filtering on prompts to maintain an effective learning range during RL stages.
Orders post-training stages based on reward reliability, transitioning systematically from hard verifiable rewards to soft judge-based signals.
Outperforms the official GLM-4.5-Air post-trained release using public data without an in-house distillation teacher.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that competitive post-training performance on large mixture-of-experts models can be fully reproduced using public data and open-source infrastructure without human labels.

papers.title: Controlling Backchannels in Streamable Full-duplex Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced a lightweight backchannel head that uses hidden states from full-duplex spoken dialogue models to predict and force-decode backchannel timing via a tunable threshold.
key_points: A lightweight backchannel head predicts backchannel start timing using internal hidden states of full-duplex models.
Force-decoding of backchannels occurs when the predicted probability crosses a user-defined, tunable threshold.
The approach generalizes across model scales, tested on 1B (F-Actor) and 7B (PersonaPlex) architectures.
Probing shows hidden states anticipate human backchannel timing, and human evaluators rated generated backchannels as on par with real ones.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables precise control over natural, real-time conversational acknowledgements in spoken dialogue systems without requiring complex model redesigns.

papers.title: Baseline Shape Decides the Verdict: A Controlled Re-Examination of Ternary Language Models at 60K Parameters

summary.tldr: A 98-run replication at 60K parameters shows that reported advantages of routed ternary models over transformers stem from suboptimal baseline depth/width shapes rather than inductive bias, with plain gated diagonal-SSMs actually outperforming routed architectures.
key_points: Varying depth and width at a 16M-byte budget creates a 22.6% validation loss span in parameter-matched transformers, allowing optimal transformer shapes to tie previously published routed ternary models.
At a 130M-byte budget, a unrouted gated diagonal-SSM block outperforms the routed model by 9.1%, while the routed model's internal router concentrates weight primarily on its recurrent pathway.

Quantization penalties vary significantly across architectures (+5.3% for transformers vs. +19.5% for routed models), but transformers retain 11-22% of total parameters in unquantized positional embeddings.

A 90/10 full-precision to ternary training schedule requires a stage-2 learning rate 10x higher than peak pretraining to outperform all-ternary training; standard fine-tuning rates perform 15.3% worse.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that sub-1M parameter model evaluations are highly sensitive to shape selection and hyperparameter tuning, preventing false attributions of performance gains to specialized routing mechanisms.

papers.title: Likelihood Ranking doesn't Scale Like Prompting in LLMs

summary.tldr: Across 95 decoder-only models, accuracy from likelihood ranking of declarative statements remains stable with model scale, whereas prompted answer accuracy improves sharply with scale and instruction-tuning.
key_points: Evaluated 95 decoder-only models ranging from 0.1B to 104B parameters across 10 multiple-choice QA datasets.
Compared task-conditioned prompted answer selection against likelihood ranking of declarative statements derived from the same question-answer pairs.
Declarative-statement likelihood ranking shows a systematic performance divergence from prompting, failing to scale with parameter size or instruction-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluators cannot treat declarative statement likelihood preferences and task-conditioned prompting as interchangeable metrics, as they measure distinct aspects of LLM behavior.

papers.title: Parts-of-Speech as Emergent Categories in SAE Latent Space

summary.tldr: A study reveals Sparse AutoEncoders localize part-of-speech categories in language models as compact, distributed groups of sparse latents rather than one-to-one feature mappings.
key_points: Part-of-speech (PoS) distinctions are highly recoverable from SAE activations, but do not correspond to atomic, one-to-one latent-to-category mappings.
The recoverability of morpho-syntactic information is not reducible to lexical memorisation.
Open and Closed PoS classes exhibit substantially different latent encoding structures.
PoS categories are supported by compact, stable groups of sparse latents that show overlap between syntactically related categories on held-out data.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding that SAEs represent grammar via distributed latent groups rather than single features helps researchers build better interpretability models for neural network representations.

papers.title: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination

summary.tldr: Rolling-WAM accelerates robotic visual-action world models by distributing joint video-action denoising across successive replanning cycles using a sliding window and rolling noise schedule.
key_points: Distributes joint video-action denoising across replanning cycles using a sliding window of video-action chunks at staggered noise levels.
Fully denoises the imminent action chunk for immediate execution while partially refining future visual-action chunks.
Carries evolving visual-action context across chunk boundaries as the sliding window advances with new camera observations.
Eliminates the need to denoise the full prediction horizon from scratch, achieving a 4.5x steady-state replanning speedup over standard joint WAMs.
Validated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces action generation latency in World Action Models, enabling faster closed-loop control for real-time robotic manipulation.

papers.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced VeriSpeak, a benchmark of 3,879 spoken claims, revealing that Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) struggle with a text-speech modality gap and require retrieval paired with explicit reasoning to effectively fact-check speech.
key_points: VeriSpeak contains 3,879 balanced true/false spoken claims covering temporal, geographical, and relational facts.
LALMs exhibit a text-speech modality gap, performing significantly worse on spoken claims compared to identical written claims.
Retrieval alone yields limited accuracy gains because LALMs frequently conflate retrieved textual evidence with the spoken claim.
Combining retrieval with explicit reasoning in a thinking-tuned LALM achieved 86.1% verification accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: Detecting audio misinformation requires LALMs to go beyond speech recognition and integrate structured, grounded reasoning over retrieved textual evidence.

papers.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records

summary.tldr: Researchers developed and clinician-validated an automated framework that generates the Benchmark for Retrieving Information in EHRs (BRIE), a continuously maintainable evaluation dataset derived from longitudinal EHR notes.
key_points: Nineteen clinicians validated the automated generator to construct the BRIE benchmark from patient notes.
Evaluation of nine LLMs across five inference strategies revealed frequent omissions of clinically critical information during multi-document and multi-encounter synthesis.
The validated generator creates multiple valid answers to capture clinician reasoning variations and continuously refreshes content to prevent benchmark leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: Automated, validated benchmark generation enables continuous, leakage-proof evaluation of clinical LLMs on complex patient record retrieval tasks without relying on static datasets.

papers.title: Does a model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate do any work?

summary.tldr: Inserting a model's stated missing fact into a rejected candidate profile significantly increases its selection odds over an irrelevant sentence control under greedy decoding, demonstrating that self-generated explanations reflect actionable decision drivers.
key_points: Testing six open models on 2WikiMultihopQA showed that supplying a named missing fact to a rejected candidate's profile increased selection odds versus an irrelevant control (odds ratio 3.57 [1.54, 8.26], Holm p=0.0210).
Placing the identical irrelevant sentence at the named rival moved the model's choice significantly more than placing it at an unmentioned third option (Holm p=0.0008).
Single-token probability reads disagreed in direction with free-text choices for the primary contrast, challenging single-token evaluation methods.

String-rule validation identified eight parser defects, including a choice-parsing bug that misidentified rejected options in 17.1% of adjudicable responses and would have falsely reported six surviving contrasts instead of four.
summary.why_it_matters: This research shows that LLM explanations for candidate rejections are not purely hallucinatory and correspond to real, leverageable features driving model selection logic.

papers.title: GRASP: Generating, Revising, and Assessing for Strategic Planning with Agentic AI

summary.tldr: GRASP is a strategy-aware, multi-stage planning framework that decouples task planning across context-isolated modules to generate high-quality natural language executable plans for complex tasks.
key_points: GRASP decouples planning into three specialized modules: GenPlan (global macro-guidelines), RevPlan (localized strategy exploration in isolated contexts), and VerPlan (multi-criteria trajectory evaluation).
The framework eliminates performance degradation in multi-task scaling, maintaining flat accuracy curves in interleaved dual-task environments with up to a 16.7% gain over direct LLM planners.
GRASP achieves accuracy improvements over direct LLM planners on ZebraLogic (~30.8%), Natural Plan Calendar Scheduling (~12.4%), and SciBench Math.
By using context isolation and strict macro-regularization, GRASP outperforms frontier reasoning models like GPT-5-mini by 14.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: By preventing performance collapse during complex, multi-task scaling, GRASP enables LLMs to execute highly intricate, multi-step natural language plans reliably.

papers.title: EnigmaForge: The Question Is Hidden in the Story

summary.tldr: EnigmaForge is a novel benchmark that hides SAT-verified logic puzzles inside generated narrative documents without explicitly providing the target question to the model.
key_points: Puzzles are embedded in narrative texts (letters, receipts, logs) with unique solutions verified by a SAT solver and ablation certificates ensuring all clues are required.
Evaluated 25 frontier models across 600 instances (17,400 scored records) under three matched conditions to measure 'intuition' (discovering the question) versus world reconstruction.
Revealed a 22x performance spread in intuition compared to a 1.6x spread in fact recovery, with the second-best fact recovery model ranking fourteenth overall.
Observed counterintuitive behavior, including one model performing better without the explicit question and others failing due to upstream content filter blocks.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes critical gaps in model reasoning and task discovery that standard direct-question benchmarks fail to measure, while avoiding dataset contamination via infinite procedural generation.

papers.title: HEXIS: Compiling Skills into Extended Finite State Machines

summary.tldr: HEXIS compiles agent skills into extended finite state machines (EFSMs), decoupling control flow from task reasoning to enforce execution structure and reduce LLM generation overhead.
key_points: HEXIS maps skill clauses and tool interfaces into state operations, local instructions, data bindings, and explicit transition conditions.
An incremental compiler aligns development traces with existing states to refine connections, add missing operations, and resolve dependencies.
State updates require static validation and successful replay of current and previously accepted execution traces.
Evaluation across four benchmarks shows a 16.1 percentage point average success rate improvement over Skill + ReAct.
Using Qwen3.8-27B, HEXIS decreases execution token consumption by 38.4% to 88.9% across benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: By enforcing deterministic control flow via state machines, agents reliably follow prescribed multi-step procedures while significantly cutting LLM token costs.

security.title: AERIAL: Adversarial Evaluation of Robustness in Accuracy-Preserving Low-Precision EEG Decoders

summary.tldr: AERIAL evaluates EEG decoders on BCI Competition IV-2a, demonstrating that accuracy-preserving compression (INT8 PTQ/QAT, 50% pruning) does not improve direct PGD adversarial robustness despite pruning reducing bidirectional transfer efficiency.
key_points: Evaluated FP32, 50% pruned (P50), INT8 PTQ, and INT8 QAT versions of EEGNet and ShallowConvNet across 9 subjects and 3 seeds.
At perturbation epsilon=0.005, EEGNet PGD accuracy stays at 22-24% across all FP32, P50, PTQ, and QAT models, showing no gain in direct robustness.
P50 pruning reduces bidirectional transfer efficiency to 0.963/0.928 (FP32 to P50 / P50 to FP32), whereas INT8 PTQ maintains high transfer efficiency at 0.994/0.997.
Simulated quantization aligns with native TensorRT hardware deployment, showing 95-98% agreement in clean and adversarial predictions.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that direct adversarial robustness, transferability, and hardware deployment efficiency are decoupled properties in compressed BCI models, meaning compression cannot be relied upon to mitigate direct attacks.

security.title: Blockchain-Enabled Artificial Intelligence and AI Agents for Secure Data Sharing and Cybersecurity Applications

summary.tldr: A meta-synthesis introduces a layered reference architecture uniting blockchain immutability, smart contracts, and multi-agent LLM pipelines to secure AI lifecycle data, anomaly detection, and automated vulnerability patching.
key_points: Synthesizes research across adversarial machine learning, cloud AI anomaly detection, and automated LLM vulnerability patching to resolve trust failures in decentralized AI.
Proposes a layered reference architecture integrating adversarially hardened models, blockchain-anchored data provenance, and smart-contract-governed multi-agent remediation.
Identifies unresolved operational bottlenecks including blockchain scalability, privacy-transparency trade-offs, and autonomous agent governance.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a unified structural blueprint for using decentralized blockchain ledgers to verify data provenance and govern autonomous multi-agent AI decisions in production-critical cybersecurity systems.

security.title: When Temporal Perturbations Act Like Sensor Biases: Label-Free Auditing of Wearable Activity Recognizers

summary.tldr: SpectrumAudit is a label-free auditing method that uses phase-randomized stimuli on held-out calibration windows to isolate and evaluate whether wearable HAR model vulnerabilities stem from persistent DC sensor offsets or AC variation.
key_points: Evaluates frozen victim models by selecting a phase-randomized full-window stimulus and replaying its exact DC projection and budget-constrained zero-mean residual without refitting.
Tested across 27 victim models spanning three datasets and three backbones, achieving three-phase robust accuracy drops ranging from 2.87 to 40.83 percentage points.
Under a fixed replay budget, DC offsets proved more damaging than AC signals on 24 of 27 victims and accounted for at least 90% of the total accuracy drop on 22 of 27 victims.
In a held-out UTD-MHAD evaluation, the selected waveform degraded accuracy by 13.49 pp and macro-F1 by 11.68 pp, compared to a -0.66 pp change for matched random baseline perturbations.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that apparent temporal vulnerabilities in wearable HAR models are often driven primarily by static sensor biases, allowing developers to audit model robustness without labeled data.

security.title: Unmasking Shortcut Learning in IoT Intrusion Detection: A Forensic, Multi-Paradigm Evaluation of Feature Dependence and Data Leakage

summary.tldr: A forensic evaluation of the CyberFlowIoT-GICAP benchmark reveals that high IoT intrusion detection performance often stems from shortcut learning, such as raw timestamp artifacts and leaky random-flow data splits.
key_points: Using purely statistical flow behavior (Fbehav), LightGBM, Random Forest, and Deep MLP achieved identical Macro-F1 (~92.58%), showing performance is bound by feature representation rather than model complexity.
Adding raw timestamps (Ftstamp) boosted nonlinear tree-based models to 99.28% Macro-F1 while linear models remained at 90.62%, demonstrating that decision trees exploit temporal dataset shortcuts.
Attack detectability is asymmetric: high-rate attacks maintain >99.8% recall on behavioral features alone, whereas DNS Beaconing recall drops to 0.00% without contextual features.
Conventional random-flow splitting artificially inflates attack recall by up to 14.00% compared to PCAP-disjoint splits due to session-level data leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: Reported near-perfect IoT intrusion detection metrics may fail in real-world deployments if models rely on temporal shortcuts and cross-session data leakage rather than true attack behaviors.

security.title: "What I See is What I Hear": Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Hearing Abilities

summary.tldr: A study of 80 participants reveals that d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing populations are less accurate at detecting audiovisual deepfakes than hearing individuals, driven by higher false-positive rates on authentic media.
key_points: In an 80-participant study, d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) individuals achieved lower overall detection accuracy (76.4%) compared to hearing persons (88.0%, p<.001).
DHH participants exhibited a significantly higher false positive rate (29.7%) on authentic media compared to hearing participants (11.2%).
Audio-only manipulation detection varied widely by group: hearing persons scored 90.3%, hard-of-hearing scored 90.0%, cochlear implant users scored 79.4%, and d/Deaf participants scored 41.2%.
Audiovisual manipulation detection accuracy clustered between 84% and 87% across all hearing ability groups.
summary.why_it_matters: Audiovisual deepfakes pose asymmetrical security and misinformation risks to d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing users, underscoring the necessity for accessible defense mechanisms tailored to diverse perceptual abilities.
